charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

turnoverSpend.title: Table turnover rate & average spend per guest
turnoverSpend.content:
Table turnover rate is how many times per day, on average, each table is seated and served -- the core throughput measure for a dine-in restaurant chain. Average spend per guest is RMB revenue per diner, the pricing/mix counterpart.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: turnover fell from 4.1x/day in FY2024 to 3.9x/day in FY2025 and has not recovered in H1 FY2026, a multi-year downtrend management attributes to intensified competition from value-oriented challengers and delivery platforms. Average spend has stayed roughly flat (~RMB97-98), so the revenue hit is a traffic problem, not a pricing one.

What to watch:

  • Any stabilisation or further decline in turnover -- it is the single metric both bull and bear cases hinge on
  • Spend per guest falling alongside turnover, which would signal discounting rather than just softer traffic

sameStore.title: Same-store sales growth & same-store count
sameStore.content:
Same-store sales growth is the YoY change in revenue from restaurants open in both periods being compared, stripping out the effect of new openings or closures. Same-store count is how many restaurants qualify for that comparison.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: same-store sales fell ~6.7% in FY2025 (guest visits down 7.5% to 383.9 million) and a further 1.3% in H1 FY2026 -- a smaller decline, but still a decline, after several consecutive down years.

What to watch:

  • Whether the H1 FY2026 deceleration in the decline (-1.3% vs -6.7%) continues into FY2026, consistent with management's 2027 reacceleration target
  • Same-store count shrinking (85 restaurants proactively closed/relocated in FY2025) alongside sales, which would flatter the per-store trend

storeCount.title: Total restaurant count
storeCount.content:
Store count is the total number of operating restaurants (predominantly self-operated Haidilao, plus a deliberately small franchise base).

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the network shrank from 1,322 restaurants at H1 FY2025 to 1,290 at H1 FY2026 as management proactively closed or relocated underperforming sites -- a disciplined response to falling turnover rather than distress, but it caps revenue growth from store count alone.

What to watch:

  • Net openings turning positive again, which management has guided toward accelerating versus 2026
  • Store count falling faster than same-store sales recover, which would mean footprint discipline is outpacing the demand recovery

revenueMix.title: Haidilao dine-in vs delivery revenue
revenueMix.content:
Haidilao dine-in revenue is the core table-service brand, still the large majority of the total. Delivery revenue is the takeaway/single-serving business (including the 'rice-bowl' fast-food format) that management is scaling as a growth pillar alongside ~20 'Pomegranate Plan' sub-brands.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: delivery revenue grew +111.9% in FY2025 and +121.2% in H1 FY2026 to RMB2,051.4m (9.2% of revenue, up from 4.5%), even as core Haidilao dine-in revenue declined -- the clearest offset to the same-store sales story above.

What to watch:

  • Whether delivery's growth rate decelerates as it scales off its now-larger base
  • Delivery and sub-brand expansion carry lower margins and higher platform/marketing costs, so revenue mix shift alone does not guarantee margin recovery

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Haidilao International Holding Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
